headline_marked: At least 14 [[injured in Jubo Dal-Chhatra Dal clashes]] in Dhaka's New Market
headline: At least 14 injured in Jubo Dal-Chhatra Dal clashes in Dhaka's New Market
summary: Violence erupted between the two groups over alleged extortion from footpath vendors and control of the area.
details: At least 14 people were injured in clashes between activists of Jubo Dal's New Market unit and Chhatra Dal members from Dhaka College in the New Market area on Tuesday evening.
The conflict began around 7:30 PM near Balaka Cinema Hall when Jubo Dal activists allegedly attempted to collect money from footpath vendors, which was resisted by Chhatra Dal members.
Witnesses report that a group of 40-50 people led by local Jubo Dal leaders attacked Dhaka College Chhatra Dal members using sticks and knives.
The violence spread to Bashundhara Goli near Priyangan Market, where further clashes, vandalism, and counter-attacks occurred, causing panic in the locality.
Eight injured from the Chhatra Dal side were identified, including Joint Convener Prince Khandaker and several other members.
Six injured from the Jubo Dal side were also identified, including Zakir, Suman, and Shah Alam.
The injured were initially treated at Popular Hospital in Dhanmondi before several were moved to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).
Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Ramna Division Deputy Commissioner Sheikh Zahidul Islam confirmed the clashes and stated that the situation was under control by 11:30 PM.
Police are currently investigating the incident and will take legal action against those involved.
caption:
Violence erupts in Dhaka's New Market as Jubo Dal and Chhatra Dal clash over footpath vendor control.

At least 14 people were injured in clashes between activists of Jubo Dal's New Market unit and Chhatra Dal members from Dhaka College in the New Market area on Tuesday evening.

The conflict began around 7:30 PM near Balaka Cinema Hall when Jubo Dal activists allegedly attempted to collect money from footpath vendors, which was resisted by Chhatra Dal members.

Witnesses report that a group of 40-50 people led by local Jubo Dal leaders attacked Dhaka College Chhatra Dal members using sticks and knives.

The violence spread to Bashundhara Goli near Priyangan Market, where further clashes, vandalism, and counter-attacks occurred, causing panic in the locality.

Eight injured from the Chhatra Dal side were identified, including Joint Convener Prince Khandaker and several other members.

Six injured from the Jubo Dal side were also identified, including Zakir, Suman, and Shah Alam.

The injured were initially treated at Popular Hospital in Dhanmondi before several were moved to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).

Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Ramna Division Deputy Commissioner Sheikh Zahidul Islam confirmed the clashes and stated that the situation was under control by 11:30 PM.

Police are currently investigating the incident and will take legal action against those involved.

headline_marked: 10 hurt as [[JnU bus attacked by locals]] in Manikganj
headline: 10 hurt as JnU bus attacked by locals in Manikganj
summary: A Jagannath University bus was attacked in Singair, leaving students and the driver injured. Police say locals may have mistaken the bus for a vehicle involved in a separate road accident.
details: At least 10 students and the driver of a Jagannath University (JnU) bus were injured when locals attacked the vehicle in Singair upazila of Manikganj yesterday afternoon.
The incident occurred at Bandakshin Bazar when the university's "Kaliganga" bus was traveling toward Manikganj.
University officials reported that two students sustained serious injuries, including one with a head injury and another hurt by shattered glass.
The transport administrator of JnU, Dr Tarek Bin Atiq, stated that the attack followed a dispute where some students allegedly pushed an auto-rickshaw driver after the driver refused to give way.
However, Singair Police Station OC Md Mazharul Islam stated that locals may have mistaken the university bus for a vehicle involved in a separate road accident that had occurred on the same road.
The injured were given preliminary treatment at hospitals in Manikganj and Singair.
University authorities are currently coordinating with local administration to file a case against several individuals who allegedly led the attack.
